page: OVHcloud r3-64 is a memory-optimized server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC processor with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The x86_64 architecture is configured without hyperthreading, allocating a full physical core per vCPU. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a 200 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU scoring in the top 25% at 3078.58. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is also in the top 25% at 101.05 GB/sec, supported by a PassMark memory score of 2964.73. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and database operations fall within the middle 50% average tier. Text generation for small language models (135M) is strong at 293.38 tokens per second, while medium model (7B) inference speeds remain average.

The instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. However, the lack of hyperthreading and a moderate 2.3 GHz clock speed limit its multi-core compute scaling compared to compute-focused instances. The inclusion of a 200 GB NVMe SSD and strong memory write speeds makes this server suitable for in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, text processing pipelines, and moderate-scale web serving.
